documentSummary.purpose: Provide a rich human-readable System definition for Inventory 3.0 without prematurely formalizing System Identity.

documentSummary.summary: Inventory 3.0 is the principal known System serving the Inventory Management Project. Historical design records describe a mobile-friendly Google Apps Script web application using Google Sheets, event-based inventory changes, current-inventory state, product/location/SDS reference data, validation, history, and later administration/reporting. Historical July 2026 records show the System was actually built and expanded. This documentation step intentionally does not create system-identity.json or assign a SYS-###, and it does not treat historical plans as proof of current live behavior.
documentSummary.confidence: high for source-grounded semantic and historical interpretation; live implementation state requires current verification

keyPoints.title: Inventory 3.0 is a System, not the Project
keyPoints.description: Inventory 3.0 is the principal known System inside the Inventory Management Project; the two are semantically distinct.

keyPoints.title: System Identity is intentionally deferred
keyPoints.description: No system-identity.json or permanent SYS-### is created in this step.

keyPoints.title: Architecture baseline is Apps Script plus Google Sheets
keyPoints.description: The historical roadmap defines a browser → Apps Script HTML interface → Apps Script inventory services → Google Sheets datastore architecture.

keyPoints.title: Inventory changes are event-oriented
keyPoints.description: The design couples inventory-state changes with event records and prohibits direct Current Inventory changes without an event.

keyPoints.title: Inventory 2.0 history is separated
keyPoints.description: The roadmap preserves Inventory 2.0 history in Inv2_Archive while establishing new Inventory 3.0 state from verified physical counts.

keyPoints.title: Historical work shows implementation beyond the roadmap
keyPoints.description: July 2026 records describe actual Inventory 3.0 construction, product pages/filtering, and SDS integration.

keyPoints.title: Historical evidence is not live-state authority
keyPoints.description: Current deployment, source, schema, quantities, version, and tests require current verification.

keyPoints.title: Resources remain separate from System identity
keyPoints.description: Apps Script projects, workbooks, deployments, source files, datasets, and documentation should resolve through Resource authority rather than be treated as intrinsic System identity.

keyPoints.title: Next test is discovery and Viewer differentiation
keyPoints.description: The Project Definition exemplar must now prove that Project and System records are discovered and presented distinctly.

supervisor.plainLanguageSummary: Inventory 3.0 is the working inventory System inside the broader Inventory Management Project. This documentation records what the System is and what historical sources say it was designed and built to do, without claiming that every old plan still describes the live system.
supervisor.operationalImpact: Separating Project, System, Resources, and historical evidence makes future inventory work easier to resume and reduces the risk of changing the wrong artifact based on stale documentation.
supervisor.currentStatus: The System documentation layer now has a README, System Summary, and structured sidecar. A formal System Identity record is intentionally deferred.
risksOrLimitations: Current deployment/source/datastore were not reverified in this documentation step.
Permanent System ID and final System boundary remain unresolved.
supervisor.nextOperationalStep: Test documentation discovery and then reconcile live implementation Resources.

general.summary: Inventory 3.0 is the principal known System serving the Inventory Management Project. Its historical design is an event-oriented, mobile-friendly Apps Script/Google Sheets inventory application. The current documentation preserves historical implementation evidence while explicitly separating it from current live-state verification.
keyPoints: System, Project, and Resources are distinct.
No System Identity Entity Record is created yet.
Roadmap statements remain planning/design evidence unless execution is established.
Current implementation Resources must be reverified before consequential changes.

technical.summary: This sidecar structures the Inventory 3.0 System Summary using the recognized generic-document sidecar profile. It represents a document about a System, not a System Identity Entity Record.
keyPoints: current live implementation not fully reverified

projectSpecificLessons: A System can be documented richly without prematurely defining System Identity.
Historical roadmap and implementation evidence should be kept in separate epistemic categories.
Inventory 3.0's event-oriented design provides a useful boundary between current state and historical change.
generalLessons: Version-bearing System names require continuity analysis before they become stable identity.
Mutable deployments and datastores should not become intrinsic System identity.
Unchecked roadmap verification items must not be rewritten as completed tests.

recurringProblems.problem: Historical application records can be mistaken for current System truth.
recurringProblems.pattern: Roadmaps, URLs, app versions, and source-file names remain readable long after implementation changes.
